modules.name: Deliverables and hard-rules tracker
modules.design_question: Which VTC hard rules and recommended deliverables are met, missing or at risk, and how many days remain before the 30 Nov 2026 closing time?
inputs: board scene JSON and export_manifest from P13-M06

editable checklist: 6 hard rules + 20 recommended items (programme, structure and massing diagrams; wind, solar/shadow and sustainability studies; site plan; ground floor plan; typical lower/mid/upper plans; 2 sections; skyline view; mid-city view; 4 ground-level perspectives; policy reflection)
module result cards from other packets (wind, shadow, sustainability, structure, programme)
rubric gaps from P13-M07
current date and team time zone
outputs: submission_status (typed JSON: hard_rules[], coverage, missing[], days_left, blocking)
blocking_issues list that disables the export-for-upload button in P13-M06
per-item evidence links for P13-M07

parameters.name: panel_count
parameters.relationship: More boards give more room for the 20 recommended items (5 per board at 4 boards), but every JPEG must independently stay under 10 MB, so the total upload budget grows with each board.

parameters.name: recommended_item_set
parameters.relationship: Each unplaced recommended item lowers coverage. Items are tagged to jury criteria (team mapping): missing ground-level perspectives weakens human-scale evidence (40%); missing wind, solar or sustainability studies weakens design-excellence evidence (20%).

parameters.name: deadline_timestamp
parameters.relationship: Closing is 23:59 London time on 30 Nov 2026 = 15:59 Vancouver (PST). Late entries are automatically disqualified and edits after first upload need a paid reactivation, so earlier export lowers both risks.

parameters.name: file_size_margin
parameters.relationship: A bigger safety margin below 10 MB protects against MB/MiB ambiguity and portal overhead but forces lower JPEG quality or fewer pixels, which softens thin linework on the board.

parameters.name: aspect_ratio_tolerance
parameters.relationship: A2 is 420 x 594 mm (ratio 1.414); a tighter tolerance prevents stretched or cropped boards, a looser one hides layout mistakes.

metrics.name: Panel file format
metrics.good: every panel is .jpg/.jpeg
metrics.bad: any PDF, PNG, TIFF or other format
metrics.method: Check extension and JPEG magic bytes of each exported board.
metrics.basis: Buildner Terms section 4.8: each panel must be saved as JPEG; non-compliant format is a disqualification ground (sections 8.2).

metrics.name: Panel file size (hard limit)
metrics.good: <= 10 MB per panel
metrics.method: Read byte length of each exported JPEG.
metrics.basis: Terms section 4.8 sets 10 MB per panel; the brief (via team) repeats it. Unit (10^6 bytes vs MiB) is not defined in what was read.

metrics.name: Panel file size (safety target)
metrics.good: <= 9.5 x 10^6 bytes
metrics.bad: between 9.5 x 10^6 bytes and 10 MB: amber; above 10 MB: red
metrics.method: Same byte count compared with a margin that is safe under either MB definition.
metrics.basis: Team margin; editable.

metrics.name: Number of panels
metrics.good: 1 to 4 panels; project plan uses exactly 4
metrics.method: Count exported boards.
metrics.basis: Terms: the brief sets the count, from a single panel up to four; project brief facts supplied by team say four A2 boards.

metrics.name: Board aspect ratio / orientation
metrics.good: landscape, width:height = 1.414 +/- 0.005 (594 x 420 mm)
metrics.method: width_px / height_px of each JPEG.
metrics.basis: A2 = 420 x 594 mm (ISO 216) is verified; the landscape rule comes from the brief as supplied by the team; the tolerance is a team choice.

metrics.name: Language
metrics.good: all text on boards declared English
metrics.method: Manual attestation per text block (P13-M08 sets language='en').
metrics.basis: Buildner page: all information submitted by participants must be in English.

metrics.name: Recommended-item coverage
metrics.good: 20 of 20 items placed (counts met: 3 typical plans, >=2 sections, >=4 ground-level views)
metrics.bad: any category with zero items placed
metrics.method: Match checklist items to tagged board elements.
metrics.basis: Item list and minimum counts come from the brief via the team; items are 'recommended', so a gap is not a rule breach and the cut-off is a team choice.

metrics.name: Days of buffer before closing
metrics.good: >= 7 days between first complete valid export and 23:59 London time on 30 Nov
metrics.bad: <= 2 days, or any hard-rule failure within 7 days
metrics.method: deadline(Europe/London) - now; shown in London and Vancouver time.
metrics.basis: Deadline is verified; late entries are auto-disqualified (Terms section 8.4); the 7-day and 2-day buffers are team choices.

visualization: Checklist grid: 20 item rows x up to 4 board columns with green/amber/red chips; each hard rule is a pass/fail badge linked to its clause (e.g., Terms section 4.8)
Dual-timezone countdown (London / Vancouver) with milestone ticks for 29 Oct registration close, 3 Nov Q&A close, 13 Nov course core, 30 Nov submission
Four board thumbnails with ghost slots for missing items and a file-size gauge (MB against 10 MB)
modules.method: Load a versioned checklist JSON with 6 hard rules and 20 recommended items. Each item has an id, label, jury tag, minimum count and the board elements that satisfy it; elements get tags in P13-M06 (for example type=section, view=skyline). Hard rules are evaluated from the export_manifest: extension, bytes, width/height ratio, panel count, anonymity findings; language is a manual attestation. Coverage = items whose minimum count is met / 20. days_left = deadline in Europe/London minus now. Any hard-rule failure sets blocking=true. Every threshold shows its source or an amber 'team assumption' tag and can be edited; each edit is logged. When Buildner answers Q&A (closes 3 Nov 2026) a rule change is recorded as a dated changelog entry.
modules.human_judgment: Whether an item really answers the brief (a wind study must be an analysis, not a diagram label); reading the full official brief and Q&A for changes; the final upload through the Buildner portal; deciding which recommended items to omit and justify.
modules.limits: The brief PDF itself could not be opened here; board count, A2 size and weights come from team-supplied text, and the Buildner pages read do not list them. The portal may apply checks (pixel size, colour mode, MB vs MiB) that are not documented. Coverage counts presence, not quality.

modules.name: Drawing extraction (plans, sections, make2d-style linework)
modules.design_question: Can plans, sections and elevations be generated from the 3D model as clean, scaled, layered linework that fits the board and reconciles with programme areas?
inputs: Layer 0 meshes / B-reps with program tags (from imports: Rhino 3dm, OBJ, IFC, SketchUp, Revit)
storey elevations and floor-to-floor heights (programme / structure modules)
cut plane and section line definitions chosen by user
site north rotation angle (SITE packet)
target scale and frame size in mm from P13-M06
outputs: drawing_set[]: {id, type plan|section|elevation, svg, scale, cut_height, bbox_mm, layers by program tag, line classes} consumed by P13-M06
gfa_by_storey reconciliation result for programme modules
DXF/SVG export for use in Rhino/Illustrator

parameters.name: cut_height_above_floor
parameters.relationship: Plans are conventionally cut about 1.2 m (4 ft) above finished floor, showing walls, openings and columns; a cut at slab level hides openings, one above head height loses wall and door relationships.

parameters.name: section_line_position
parameters.relationship: A section through the core and public volumes shows how public-facing uses stack vertically through the tower, which the brief asks for; a section through blank floors hides it.

parameters.name: drawing_scale
parameters.relationship: Printed extent = real size / n. The 144.8 m block side is 290 mm at 1:500 but 724 mm at 1:200, which exceeds the 420 mm board height; a smaller scale frees area but shrinks annotation legibility.

parameters.name: hidden_lines_on
parameters.relationship: Hidden lines add information (below-grade volumes, stacked cores) but add clutter; Rhino Make2D puts them on separate layers so they can be dashed or switched off.

parameters.name: input_route
parameters.relationship: The mesh route projects along one axis at a time, so the model is rotated per view; the IFC route can use IfcOpenShell geometry; a Rhino Make2D result can be imported when NURBS-exact linework is needed.

parameters.name: crease_angle_threshold
parameters.relationship: UNRESOLVED: relationship between edge-angle threshold and drawing clarity on curved facades was not found in an opened source (see unresolved_relationships).

metrics.name: Plan cut height convention
metrics.good: 1.2 m (about 4 ft) above finished floor
metrics.bad: cut at slab level (0 m) or above 1.8 m
metrics.method: Compare chosen cut with the convention.
metrics.basis: Good value is the stated convention; the bad bounds are the team's reading of 'approximately'.

metrics.name: Cut-loop closure ratio
metrics.good: 100% of cut polylines closed (poche can fill)
metrics.method: closed cut loops / all cut loops after slicing Layer 0 with the cut plane.
metrics.basis: Open loops indicate non-watertight Layer 0 geometry; thresholds are team-set.

metrics.name: Drawing fits allocated frame
metrics.good: scaled bbox <= 100% of frame in both axes
metrics.method: bbox_mm = model extent / scale, compared with frame in mm on a 594 x 420 mm board.
metrics.basis: Arithmetic from the brief's site size and the A2 dimensions.

metrics.name: Segments per drawing
metrics.good: <= 250,000 line segments
metrics.method: Count after linework simplification.
metrics.basis: No published budget; chosen so rasterising a board stays fast. Tune after testing.

metrics.name: Area reconciliation with programme tags
metrics.good: |plan area - tagged GFA| <= 1% per storey
metrics.method: Sum polygon areas of cut slab loops per storey versus the Layer 0 tag totals.
metrics.basis: Team tolerance.

metrics.name: Line-weight hierarchy
metrics.good: cut > silhouette > projected edge > hidden with each step about 2:1
metrics.bad: two classes drawn at the same weight
metrics.method: Class-to-weight table rendered in the SVG stroke-width.
metrics.basis: Common drafting convention recalled from ISO 128-20 but that standard was not opened; weights are editable presets.

visualization: SVG preview with toggles per line class (cut, silhouette, crease, hidden) and per program-tag layer, poche filled with the programme colour
Plan with cut-line markers and rotated site north arrow; scale bar
Board-frame overlay showing the drawing at 1:n inside the allocated rectangle with an overflow warning in red
modules.method: 1) Normalise Layer 0 to indexed meshes (B-rep tessellated). 2) Plan: slice meshes with a horizontal plane at the cut height, chain intersection segments into polylines, close loops, and fill them as poche; project the visible geometry below the cut with BVH-based edge projection. 3) Section/elevation: rotate the scene so the view axis matches the projection axis, clip at the section plane, repeat. 4) Classify lines as cut, silhouette, crease or hidden; remove occluded edges. 5) Output SVG layered by program tag, plus scale bar and north arrow rotated by the site angle. For IFC inputs use IfcOpenShell on a server worker; for exact NURBS linework accept Rhino Make2D output as an imported SVG/DXF. Report closure ratio, segment count and area reconciliation.
modules.human_judgment: Where to cut and section, which elements and levels represent the design, line weights, annotation and entourage, and whether the drawing actually tells the story of vertical public uses.
modules.limits: Linework comes from tessellated meshes, not NURBS, so curved facades are faceted; thin curtain-wall detail and below-slab structure are absent from Layer 0. The edge-projection library works along one axis and shows 12 open issues; performance on a 300 m tower is untested. Rhino Make2D is the quality reference.

libraries.name: three-edge-projection
libraries.role: visible edge projection and flattening to 2D line segments

libraries.name: rhino3dm
libraries.role: read .3dm geometry, layers and attributes in browser (WASM)

libraries.name: IfcOpenShell
libraries.role: IFC geometry and server-side drawing generation

libraries.name: manifold-3d
libraries.role: candidate mesh boolean/section engine (slice API not confirmed on the page read)

modules.effort: L: 8-12 person-days for mesh-based plan and section (core); +5 days for IFC hidden-line route (v1)

modules.name: Camera presets and viewpoint library
modules.design_question: From which sourced viewpoints and lenses must the tower be shown (Queen Elizabeth Park skyline, mid-city, four ground-level views), and does the design read at those distances?
inputs: site location and ground elevation, terrain and context models (SITE packet)
tower heights and massing from Layer 0
site north rotation angle
view-cone geometry if available from SITE packet
sun date/time from CLIM packet for lighting
outputs: camera_preset[]: {name, position, target, hfov, roll, shift, viewpoint_source, eye_height} consumed by P13-M04, P13-M05, P13-M06 and CLIM image exports
tower_share_of_frame per preset
compass-labelled overlay data (Stanley Park, BC Place, Entertainment District, Burrard Inlet/North Shore Mountains)

parameters.name: viewpoint_position_and_elevation
parameters.relationship: Queen Elizabeth Park is listed at 49.2422 N 123.1150 W (Little Mountain 49.2417 N 123.1133 W) about 125 m above sea level; a high viewpoint puts more of the tower above the horizon and shows it against context rather than sky only.

parameters.name: viewing_distance
parameters.relationship: Apparent height = atan(height difference / distance). Illustration: a 300 m tower at 5 km subtends about 3.4 degrees, so doubling distance halves its size in frame and forces a longer lens or a crop.

parameters.name: focal_length_equivalent
parameters.relationship: Horizontal field = 2 x atan(18/f): 50 mm gives 39.6 degrees, 85 mm gives 23.9 degrees. Longer lenses enlarge the distant tower in frame but narrow the visible context.

parameters.name: eye_height
parameters.relationship: Ground-level views at about 1.6 m show canopies and podium frontage at pedestrian scale, the scale the human-scale criterion judges; higher cameras read as aerial views.

parameters.name: view_cone_status
parameters.relationship: The City keeps four Queen Elizabeth Park cones (3.2.1 to 3.2.4); the Higher Buildings Policy allows only select sites to encroach through a special review, so a skyline image must honestly show any encroachment.

parameters.name: site_north_rotation
parameters.relationship: The site plan's north arrow is rotated from the street grid, so view azimuths and compass labels must use the rotated north or the labels will point to the wrong landmarks.

metrics.name: Tower share of frame height (QE Park skyline)
metrics.good: >= 10% of image height
metrics.method: Project tower top and base to the image plane; (top_y - base_y)/frame height; auto-suggest focal length to reach the target.
metrics.basis: Team legibility target; no source gives a value.

metrics.name: Viewpoint position error versus the City's designated origin
metrics.good: within the tolerance of the origin published in the Public Views Guidelines (value not obtained)
metrics.bad: viewpoint not traceable to a published origin
metrics.method: Distance between preset and published origin once obtained.
metrics.basis: The 2024 Public Views Guidelines PDF returned HTTP 403; origin, azimuth and height not read.

metrics.name: Number of ground-level perspectives
metrics.method: Count presets of type ground.
metrics.basis: Brief recommends at least four ground-level perspectives (as supplied by team).

metrics.name: Ground-level eye height
metrics.method: Camera z minus local ground z.
metrics.basis: Common adult eye height; team preset, editable.

metrics.name: Vertical convergence
metrics.good: verticals within 0.5 degrees of vertical (shift lens, zero pitch)
metrics.method: Check camera pitch/roll and lens shift.
metrics.basis: Architectural-visualisation convention; team preset.

visualization: Plan map with north arrow (rotated), a wedge for each camera and a dashed line of sight to the tower top
Elevation profile from the viewpoint to the site: terrain line, horizon, tower silhouette, view-cone ceiling if available
Thumbnail grid with 'tower % of frame' badge and burned-in compass labels
modules.method: Convert viewpoint lat/lon to the project's local frame (WGS84 to UTM zone 10N, EPSG:32610) with proj4js, add the terrain elevation from the SITE packet and the eye height. Point the camera at the tower centroid, set roll to zero and use lens shift to keep verticals vertical. Choose focal length so the tower share of frame meets the target, then ray-cast from the camera to tower top and base against context meshes to flag occlusion by existing towers. Ground-level presets are placed at the four site edges named in the brief (arterial side, retail high street, lane or mid-block connection, transit plaza and below-grade station entrance), eye height 1.6 m. Output camera JSON and burned-in compass labels using the rotated north.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the mid-city viewpoint, composition, season and time of day; confirming the QE Park position against the City's designated origin; deciding which four ground-level views best show the public realm.
modules.limits: Terrain and city context must come from the SITE packet. The exact QE Park view-cone origin, azimuth and height were not obtained (City hosts returned 403). Tree canopy and haze at the park are not modelled. The brief does not define the mid-city viewpoint.

libraries.name: proj4js
libraries.license: not stated on the page read; check LICENSE.md

depends_on: SITE packet: site, terrain, context, north angle

modules.name: Viewport conditioning capture (depth, line, segmentation)
modules.design_question: Which exact structural guides (clay beauty, depth, line, program-colour segmentation) can be rendered from Layer 0 so AI renderings stay registered to the massing?
inputs: camera_preset from P13-M03
Layer 0 and context meshes with program tags
palette mapping program tag to flat colour
target pixel size
outputs: conditioning_pack: {beauty_png, depth_png, line_png, seg_png, palette_json, camera_json, sha256} consumed by P13-M05
pixel-aligned tower mask used by the fidelity check

parameters.name: capture_size
parameters.relationship: gpt-image sizes need multiples of 16, ratio <= 3:1, edges <= 3840 px and 655,360-8,294,400 pixels; above 2560x1440 is experimental. Larger captures keep thin features but raise token cost.

parameters.name: depth_range_normalisation
parameters.relationship: The diffusers examples min-max normalise depth to 0-1 per image, so the near/far range sets how many grey levels the tower receives; a range spanning the whole city leaves the tower few levels.

parameters.name: line_threshold
parameters.relationship: The diffusers example uses Canny thresholds 100 and 200; lower thresholds keep more edges and tighten structural control on the result, higher ones keep only strong outlines.

parameters.name: segmentation_palette
parameters.relationship: The original ControlNet segmentation model expects ADE20K classes; a custom programme palette needs a prompt legend or a fine-tuned model to be interpreted correctly.

parameters.name: controlnet_conditioning_scale
parameters.relationship: In diffusers examples a scale of 0.5 is used; higher values follow the guide image more strictly, lower values give the prompt more freedom and risk geometry drift.

metrics.name: Size rule compliance (OpenAI route)
metrics.good: all five size rules satisfied
metrics.method: Validate width, height, ratio and pixel count before sending.
metrics.basis: OpenAI image-generation guide size constraints.

metrics.name: Registration between passes
metrics.good: 0 px offset (same camera, same render call)
metrics.method: Compare silhouette of the depth, line and segmentation passes.
metrics.basis: By construction; checks protect against resize or crop mistakes.

metrics.name: Tagged-pixel completeness
metrics.good: 100% of tower pixels carry a program tag
metrics.method: Count pixels of the 'unknown' colour inside the tower mask.
metrics.basis: Team threshold.

metrics.name: Pack completeness
metrics.good: depth + line + segmentation + beauty present (ControlNet route); beauty present (OpenAI route)
metrics.method: Check files and sidecar JSON.
metrics.basis: Route requirements from the ControlNet guide and OpenAI edit endpoint.

visualization: 2x2 contact sheet of beauty, depth (grey ramp with near/far legend), line and segmentation (palette legend by programme)
Opacity slider that overlays any pass on the beauty capture
modules.method: From the chosen camera render four passes with identical size and camera in three.js: (1) clay beauty with ambient occlusion and the sun from CLIM; (2) linear depth normalised between near and far values set around tower plus site; (3) line pass from depth/normal discontinuities plus crease edges; (4) ID pass with flat unlit colour per program tag, no anti-aliasing so tags survive. Save PNGs and a JSON sidecar with camera, palette, tag counts and SHA-256. Validate size rules before any API call. For fidelity checks later, depth can be re-estimated from the AI output with a small monocular model and compared with the exact depth pass.
modules.human_judgment: Which context to include or hide, time of day and sun angle, which landmarks must remain recognisable, and whether the clay capture is a fair representation of the design.
modules.limits: Programme tags are the only semantic classes; trees, water and street furniture have none. ControlNet checkpoints in the cited examples are trained near 512-1024 px, far below board resolution. OpenAI image edits take reference images, not strict control maps, so passes beyond the beauty capture may be only weak hints.

modules.name: Style selection and AI rendering pipeline
modules.design_question: Which style and engine give faithful, site-specific, non-generic renderings from the conditioning pack, at what cost, with what fidelity checks and with honest AI labelling?
inputs: conditioning_pack from P13-M04
camera_preset metadata
programme and materials from ADVANCED mode
style preset and structured prompt fields
cultural and ecological cues from CULT/ECOL packets
engine choice and API credentials (user-supplied, never stored in the module)
outputs: render_asset: {image, role skyline|midcity|ground, camera_id, engine, model_snapshot, prompt, seed, size, quality, cost_usd, fidelity{silhouette_iou, edge_match}, ai_label{iptc_digital_source_type, caption}, accepted}
ai_ledger entry per call consumed by P13-M08 and P13-M06

parameters.name: engine
parameters.relationship: OpenAI route: image edit from reference images, no explicit depth/line control. Open route (SDXL/Flux + ControlNet via ComfyUI or diffusers): explicit conditioning scale and local control, but licences and GPU needs differ.

parameters.name: openai_model
parameters.relationship: gpt-image-2.5-sunburst is described for editing precision, gpt-image-2.5-flare for fast everyday generation, gpt-image-2 remains available; all three share token prices. Snapshot ids pin results for reproducibility.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.relationship: Higher quality raises output tokens and cost; earlier models produced 272, 1,056 and 4,160 output tokens at 1024x1024 for low, medium, high, roughly a four-fold step each. Tokens for the 2.5 models are not published in what was read.

parameters.name: size
parameters.relationship: Custom sizes must be multiples of 16 with ratio <= 3:1; above 2560x1440 is experimental. A 3840x2160 output is about 164 px/inch across a 594 mm board, so large heroes may need upscaling.

parameters.name: mask_region
parameters.relationship: Masked edits let sky, trees or foreground change while the tower stays; masking is prompt-based and may not follow the mask shape exactly, so protected pixels can still shift.

parameters.name: conditioning_scale (open route)
parameters.relationship: Higher scale keeps output closer to the line/depth guide, lower scale gives more stylistic freedom; the diffusers examples use 0.5. Architecture-specific tuning evidence was not found.

parameters.name: style_preset
parameters.relationship: Style changes how generic an image looks; the brief says to avoid generic, placeless design, so presets should be anchored by site cues (City in Nature, mountains, water) chosen by the team. Effect on jury score is not evidenced.

parameters.name: moderation
parameters.relationship: 'auto' applies standard filtering; blocked requests return moderation_blocked and must not be retried without changing the inputs.

metrics.name: Tower silhouette IoU (fidelity)
metrics.method: Segment the AI output (tower class) and compare with the tower mask from the conditioning segmentation pass.
metrics.basis: No published benchmark for architectural fidelity; team thresholds, tune on pilot renders.

metrics.name: Line agreement
metrics.good: >= 0.80 of conditioning line pixels within 3 px of an output edge
metrics.method: Edge-detect the output and compute proportion of guide-line pixels with an output edge within a tolerance.
metrics.basis: Team thresholds.

metrics.name: Storey / bay count match (hero views)
metrics.good: visible storey lines equal the model
metrics.method: Human tick in the review step, assisted by overlaying the model's floor lines.
metrics.basis: A rendering must not misrepresent the design; team rule.

metrics.name: Cost per accepted image
metrics.good: <= team budget (default US$ 2.00, editable)
metrics.method: (text_in x 5 + image_in x 8 + image_out x 30) / 10^6 per image at standard rates; batch rates are half; read token counts from the response usage when available.
metrics.basis: Token rates verified; the usage field names were not seen in the docs read; the budget is a team value.

metrics.name: AI label and ledger coverage
metrics.good: 100% of AI-derived images carry a visible caption and a ledger entry
metrics.method: Join render_asset records with board placements.
metrics.basis: Good practice from journal disclosure rules and EU Article 50 principles; Buildner's terms read contain no AI rule.

metrics.name: Provenance signal present in API output
metrics.good: C2PA and/or SynthID detected on the returned image
metrics.method: Read manifest with a C2PA reader; check OpenAI's verification page manually.
metrics.basis: Help-centre text (not opened; search excerpt) says API images carry C2PA metadata and SynthID, with coverage varying and metadata strippable.

visualization: Side-by-side slider of conditioning beauty and AI output with a difference overlay (line mismatches in red, silhouette misses in amber)
Metric badges (IoU, line agreement, cost) each linked to the threshold source or an amber 'team assumption' tag
Gallery with 'AI' badge, model snapshot, prompt and cost on each card; running cost meter
modules.method: 1) User picks a camera preset, style preset and engine. 2) A structured prompt is built from fields (programme to materials, season, time of day, weather, entourage) with a block-list: no logos, signage, team names, real-person likenesses, or imitation of Indigenous art. 3) OpenAI route: POST /v1/images/edits with model, prompt, image[] = clay capture (optionally depth/line as extra references), size, quality. Open route: submit a ComfyUI workflow to /prompt (ControlNet depth + line) or call diffusers; keep the seed. 4) Compute fidelity metrics against the conditioning pack. 5) Write a ledger entry (model snapshot, parameters, prompt, input/output hashes, date). 6) Attach label text and IPTC digital source type. 7) Human accepts or rejects; rejected renders stay in the ledger.
modules.human_judgment: Whether to use AI imagery at all; style and prompt wording; accepting or rejecting each image; checking that nothing misrepresents the design; cultural sensitivity and Indigenous perspectives; checking rights and tool terms, since Buildner advises against treating AI images as sole work.
modules.limits: OpenAI image edits are not geometry-locked: the guide notes weak precision in layout-sensitive compositions and text, and complex prompts can take up to two minutes. Model names were read from OpenAI pages through a summarising fetch and look unusual; confirm before coding. FLUX.1 [dev] weights are under a non-commercial licence; SDXL is released under OpenRAIL++ for research-oriented use.

libraries.name: FLUX.1 [dev] weights
libraries.role: open image model (outputs may be used commercially per the model card)

modules.effort: M: 4-5 person-days for the OpenAI route (core); +5-8 days for the ComfyUI/ControlNet adapter and fidelity metrics (v1)

modules.name: Board layout engine and export
modules.design_question: How should drawings, images, diagrams and text be composed on up to four A2 landscape boards, and does each exported JPEG pass every Buildner hard rule?
inputs: drawing_set from P13-M02
render_asset from P13-M05 and CLIM/ENER/STRC diagram exports
text_blocks and captions from P13-M08
checklist and blocking list from P13-M01
team deny-list of identifying strings (names, university, emails, logos)
outputs: board_jpeg[1..4] (JPEG, sRGB, metadata scrubbed, neutral filenames)
export_manifest: {bytes, px, dpi, ratio, sha256, checks[], anonymity_findings[]} consumed by P13-M01
board_proof.pdf at 594 x 420 mm for team review and printing only

parameters.name: export_dpi
parameters.relationship: Pixels = mm / 25.4 x dpi: 150 dpi = 3508 x 2480; 200 dpi = 4677 x 3307; 300 dpi = 7016 x 4961. Higher dpi keeps hairlines crisp but pushes JPEG bytes toward the 10 MB cap.

parameters.name: jpeg_quality_search
parameters.relationship: The encoder searches the highest quality that keeps the file under target; lower quality shrinks bytes but adds ringing around thin linework and small type. The curve depends on content, so it is measured not predicted.

parameters.name: type_scale
parameters.relationship: At fit-to-width on a 1920 px screen, 594 mm = 3.23 px/mm, so 2.5 mm lettering is about 8 px and 3.5 mm about 11 px; smaller text becomes unreadable if the jury views boards on screen (assumed).

parameters.name: placed_image_scale
parameters.relationship: Effective resolution = image width in px / placed width in inches; enlarging an AI render past its native pixels lowers effective dpi and softens detail.

parameters.name: metadata_policy
parameters.unit: strip all | keep IPTC source type
parameters.relationship: Creator names, software strings and manifests can reveal authors; the terms bar identifying marks. ExifTool warns that stripping is not guaranteed complete, so the exported file is re-scanned.

parameters.name: ai_label_placement
parameters.relationship: A visible caption beside each AI-derived image gives the 'clear and distinguishable' disclosure that EU Article 50 expects for synthetic images; hiding it in metadata alone is fragile because metadata can be stripped.

metrics.name: Bytes per board
metrics.good: <= 9.5 x 10^6 bytes
metrics.method: Measure final file; loop quality and pixel size until under target.
metrics.basis: Terms section 4.8 limit is verified; the 9.5 x 10^6 target margin is a team choice.

metrics.name: File format
metrics.good: JPEG
metrics.method: Magic bytes and extension.
metrics.basis: Terms section 4.8.

metrics.name: Pixel ratio
metrics.method: width_px / height_px.
metrics.basis: A2 dimensions verified; tolerance team-set.

metrics.name: Effective resolution of each placed raster
metrics.good: >= 150 px/inch at 594 mm board width
metrics.method: native px / placed inches for every image.
metrics.basis: Team print/screen target; no jury requirement found.

metrics.name: Smallest text height
metrics.good: >= 3.5 mm on the board (about 11 px at 1920 px width)
metrics.method: Scan text frames and SVG text; report min cap height.
metrics.basis: 2.5 mm and 3.5 mm are nominal lettering sizes in the technical-lettering series; they are not a legibility rule for boards.

metrics.name: Anonymity findings
metrics.good: 0 findings in file name, EXIF/XMP/ICC, and OCR text matching the deny-list
metrics.method: Re-read the exported JPEG metadata and OCR it for deny-list strings.
metrics.basis: Terms section 5.1: entries must not show identifying marks; scan method is the team's design.

metrics.name: AI-derived images with visible label
metrics.method: Compare render_asset list with placements and caption frames.
metrics.basis: Disclosure practice; Buildner terms read contain no AI rule.

visualization: WYSIWYG board canvas with snap grid and four-board overview strip
Overlays: text-size heat map (red below 2.5 mm), per-image effective-dpi flags, file-size gauge (MB vs 10 MB), anonymity findings pinned to the image
Side-by-side 'what the jury sees' preview at 1920 px width and at 100% zoom
modules.method: Boards are stored as JSON scenes (frames, SVG drawings, raster images, text blocks) in millimetres. Each scene is composed into one SVG of 594 x 420 mm, rasterised with resvg at the chosen dpi, and encoded to JPEG with MozJPEG (through jSquash or sharp) in sRGB. A loop lowers quality from 95 toward 70, then reduces pixel dimensions, until the file is under the target. Metadata is stripped and the result is re-read with ExifTool; tesseract.js OCRs the raster for deny-list strings. A proof PDF (1683.8 x 1190.6 pt) is built with pdf-lib for printing only. The manifest (bytes, pixels, ratio, hash, checks) is returned to P13-M01. Export is blocked while blocking=true.
modules.human_judgment: Composition, narrative order, visual hierarchy and what to show; final QA at 100% zoom; deciding whether captions or disclosures are placed well; the upload to the Buildner portal and the final anonymity check.
modules.limits: Buildner pixel, colour-mode and MB/MiB rules are not documented in the pages read. Browser canvas size limits were not verified, so use the WASM or server path. JPEG is lossy and fine linework suffers near the size cap. PDF is a proof only: the terms require JPEG panels. Fonts must be licensed or open.

modules.name: Jury-criteria self-assessment rubric
modules.design_question: How well do the design and board set address each weighted jury criterion, and what cited evidence supports every self-score?
inputs: jury criteria and sub-criteria with weights 40/30/20/10 (brief)
evidence links to module results from all packets, each with metric, threshold and source
board placements from P13-M06 and area share per criterion
human scores on a 0-4 scale
breach register (departures from policy and guidelines) with rationale from P13-M08
outputs: rubric_state: {scores[], evidence[], gaps[], weighted_total, attention_ratio[]} consumed by P13-M01 and P13-M08
evidence table for the policy reflection

parameters.name: criterion_weights
parameters.relationship: One point on the 0-4 scale is worth 10 points of 100 for human-scale (40%) but 2.5 points for urban integration (10%), so effort and board space should follow the weights.

parameters.name: level_descriptors
parameters.relationship: Written descriptors make scores comparable between team members; vague descriptors raise rater disagreement. The review of scoring rubrics concerns reliability and validity, but its findings were not read.

parameters.name: evidence_tier
parameters.unit: A measured | B visual | C narrative
parameters.relationship: Higher-tier evidence supports a higher score; a score of 3 or more without tier-A or tier-B evidence is flagged as unsupported (team rule).

parameters.name: board_area_share
parameters.relationship: The share of board area used for a criterion should track its weight; a 30%-weight criterion with 5% area is under-communicated, which matters because the jury sees only the boards.

parameters.name: breach_register
parameters.relationship: The brief says the jury may reward justified breaches of guidelines, so each departure needs a stated reason and evidence; unexplained departures count against the criterion they touch.

metrics.name: Weighted self-score
metrics.method: sum over criteria of weight x score/4 x 100.
metrics.basis: Weights from the brief; cut-offs are team values; the result is not a prediction of jury outcome.

metrics.name: Evidence coverage per criterion
metrics.good: >= 3 items incl. >=1 measured and >=1 visual
metrics.method: Count linked evidence by tier.
metrics.basis: Team rule supporting the course requirement to cite sources and show work.

metrics.name: Board attention ratio
metrics.method: (area share of criterion) / (weight share).
metrics.basis: Team heuristic.

metrics.name: Rater disagreement
metrics.good: |score A - score B| <= 1 on the 0-4 scale
metrics.method: Two team members score independently; compare.
metrics.basis: Team threshold; reliability literature is cited for context only.

metrics.name: Site-specific evidence count (anti-generic)
metrics.good: >= 3 items tied to the site (landscape, climate, history, Indigenous perspectives) per cultural-context sub-criterion
metrics.method: Count evidence tagged 'site-specific' by the author.
metrics.basis: The brief asks to avoid generic, placeless design; threshold is team-set.

visualization: Four-axis radar chart plus a bar whose width follows weight (40/30/20/10)
Stacked evidence bars per criterion by tier; evidence table with metric, threshold, source link
Board heat strip showing which criterion each element supports; version history of scores
modules.method: Store criteria, sub-criteria, descriptors and evidence links as data. Each evidence item points to a module id, metric name, value, threshold and source id, or to a board element. Humans enter 0-4 scores with a one-line justification. The tool computes the weighted total, tier counts, board attention ratio and flags: score >= 3 without tier-A/B evidence, criterion with zero evidence, high weight with low area share, large gap between two raters, breaches without rationale. Scores are never computed or filled by an AI; an optional assistant may only suggest which existing results could serve as evidence, and the suggestion is logged. Every threshold shows its source or an amber 'team assumption' tag.
modules.human_judgment: All scores and their interpretation, especially human-scale experience, cultural context and reconciliation, which need lived knowledge and Indigenous perspectives; deciding which breaches to make and justify; interpreting what the jury will value.
modules.limits: No published VTC scoring scale or past jury scores were found; the weights come from the brief as supplied by the team (Buildner pages read do not list them). Self-scores are biased and unvalidated against jury outcomes. The jury panel page was not opened. The rubric measures evidence coverage, not design quality.

modules.name: Writing support, authorship and AI-disclosure ledger
modules.design_question: How can the tool help the team write the policy reflection and project description from cited evidence while words and judgments stay human and every AI use is disclosed?
inputs: module results and source lists from all packets
rubric_state and breach register from P13-M07
ai_ledger entries from P13-M05
team notes and drafts typed by humans
Higher Buildings Policy documents and Public Views Guidelines (reference list)
outputs: text_blocks[]: {board_id, role policy_reflection|description|caption, text, language, claim_links[], provenance} consumed by P13-M06
ai_ledger (JSONL) and a plain-language AI-use statement for course submission
unsupported-claim report

parameters.name: assistance_level
parameters.relationship: L0 evidence pack only, L1 outline and questions, L2 critique of a human draft, L3 AI-drafted text (off by default). Higher levels reduce the human share of authorship and raise the disclosure and originality risk.

parameters.name: claim_traceability
parameters.relationship: Each number or policy claim must link to a module result and its source; untraceable numbers are shown as team assumptions or flagged FALSE ASSUMPTION if later disproved, so unsupported claims cannot enter boards silently.

parameters.name: governing_policy_set
parameters.relationship: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is under review (Phase 1 early directions, spring-summer 2026; no update adopted); Public Views Guidelines were approved 10 July 2024. The reflection must say which document it assesses against.

parameters.name: text_length
parameters.relationship: More words per board lower the type size that fits; the board layout caps legible text, so length trades against the 2.5-3.5 mm text-height targets in P13-M06.

parameters.name: disclosure_detail
parameters.relationship: Journal-style rules require disclosing AI tool use and keep humans responsible for output; a detailed ledger makes the statement accurate and supports the course rule to show work.

parameters.name: identity_exposure
parameters.relationship: A C2PA signing certificate identifies the signer, so signing exported boards with a personal identity would conflict with anonymity; labels should use plain captions and non-identifying IPTC source-type fields.

metrics.name: Traceable-claim ratio
metrics.good: 100% of numeric claims linked to a source or flagged team assumption
metrics.method: Regex-detect numbers and policy names; check for a claim link.
metrics.basis: Course requirement to cite sources; cut-offs are team values.

metrics.name: Human-authored share of final text
metrics.good: 100% of final prose typed or edited by a team member (levels L0-L2 only)
metrics.bad: any AI-originated sentence not reviewed and disclosed
metrics.method: Compare diff log provenance tags per paragraph.
metrics.basis: Informed by journal guidance that AI is not an author and humans are accountable; not a Buildner rule.

metrics.name: AI-use ledger completeness
metrics.good: 100% of AI calls (text and image) logged with model, date, purpose, input/output hash
metrics.method: Compare API call log with ledger rows.
metrics.basis: Disclosure principle from ICMJE guidance.

metrics.name: Breach rationale coverage
metrics.good: 100% of flagged breaches have a written justification
metrics.method: Join breach register with text_blocks.
metrics.basis: Brief says justified breaches may be rewarded (as supplied by team).

metrics.name: Identifying strings in text
metrics.good: 0 matches against the deny-list
metrics.method: String match; the OCR pass in P13-M06 repeats it on the raster.
metrics.basis: Terms section 5.1 bars identifying marks.

metrics.name: IPTC source type on AI images
metrics.good: trainedAlgorithmicMedia set for generated images; compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia for edits such as inpainting
metrics.method: Read XMP of exported component images.
metrics.basis: IPTC vocabulary definitions; human decides which applies.

visualization: Three-pane editor: evidence pack with source chips; human draft with provenance underline (none = human, amber = AI-suggested); ledger timeline
Claim linter badges beside each sentence (linked, team assumption, unsupported)
Policy checklist with pass / exceed / breach per policy item and a justification field
modules.method: 1) Evidence pack: pull module results, thresholds and source citations into a collapsible panel. 2) Question templates (team-authored) prompt the writer: which policy items are met, exceeded or breached, and why. 3) A text editor records provenance per paragraph; AI features are limited to L0-L2 by default and every use writes a ledger row (model, version, date, purpose, hashes, reviewer). 4) A linter flags numbers or policy names without a claim link. 5) The tool builds captions such as 'AI-assisted image: model and snapshot, generated from a Rhino viewport capture' and sets the IPTC source type. 6) Language is attested as English. 7) Output text blocks go to P13-M06; ledger goes to the course submission.
modules.human_judgment: All prose, positions and ethical stance; whether any AI text is used; reconciliation and Indigenous perspectives, which should draw on community knowledge not generated text; the final policy reflection; the legal check on rights and tool terms; confirming the course's own AI rules.
modules.limits: No sourced benchmark defines a good policy reflection or project description. Buildner's terms contain no AI rule and its FAQ advises caution, so the team's own disclosure standard is a choice. UBC course guidance could not be opened (404). EU AI Act Article 50 is cited as a benchmark; its binding force for a Canadian entry and any later change to its application date were not checked.

change_log: R1: First specification of P13: 8 modules (M01 tracker, M02 drawing extraction, M03 camera presets, M04 conditioning capture, M05 AI render pipeline, M06 board layout and export, M07 jury rubric, M08 writing support and AI ledger).
R1: Added Buildner Terms rules not in the scope text: JPEG-only panels, 10 MB cap, portal upload only, no previous publication of visuals, no AI rule; flagged PDF-as-submission as a false assumption.
R1: Added deadline conversion (23:59 London = 15:59 Vancouver) and 40 days remaining from 21 Oct 2026.
R1: Found current OpenAI image models (gpt-image-2.5-sunburst, -flare, gpt-image-2) and token pricing; flagged names and C2PA statements as unverified.
R1: Added anonymity risks (EXIF/XMP, C2PA signer identity) and a re-scan step after metadata stripping.

R1: Research limits: the shared web-search budget ran out mid-task, so some searches were not repeated; City of Vancouver sites (vancouver.ca, guidelines.vancouver.ca, syc.vancouver.ca), the OpenAI Help Center and COPE returned 403 or 404 and are marked unopened or omitted.
notes: Research notes. Web search budget (shared) ran out partway; remaining checks used direct page fetches only. Fetches pass through a summarising model, so figures read that way (OpenAI model names, prices, size rules) should be re-checked against the live documentation before coding. All City of Vancouver policy PDFs (Higher Buildings Policy 1997, Public Views Guidelines 2024, review overview) returned HTTP 403, so view-cone details are unverified; the Higher Buildings Policy (1997) remains the policy under review (no 2026 update adopted, per the City's project page). Today's date 21 Oct 2026: 40 days to the 30 Nov 2026 closing; course core 13 Nov; v1 10 Dec. Priorities: core = M01-M06; v1 = M07-M08. Derived numbers (A2 pixels per dpi, 1:200 / 1:500 extents, angular size at 5 km, horizontal field of view per focal length, PDF points 1683.8 x 1190.6) are arithmetic from cited dimensions and are labelled as illustrations where inputs are assumed.
